answer: The Sybil defense is a per-seat stake that unlocks only after a fixed hold period. An operator cannot recycle one stake across seats, since settlement is per seat after the lock ends. A raven-clone farm of N seats ties up N stakes at once, so the attacker needs about N times the stake in idle capital, and a seat caught double-claiming forfeits its stake. Honest agents reclaim theirs at opportunity cost, while a canyon of sequential identities must each burn a lock window, so throughput scales with money, not keys. An orchard of twinned accounts stops paying once the stake tops the reward.
